  1. net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api

Choose an effect and adjust its appearance

Choose a text animation, set its colors and speed, and adjust the settings it accepts. The table shows what each built-in effect looks like. Create an effect with MovementRegistry.create, then register a formatting code when text needs to select it.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or settingArgumentsWhat it does
MovementRegistry.create(...)Effect ID and the settings in the examplesValidate and copy a nonempty palette, then construct the selected effect.
getRenderColor(original, x, y)Original RGB color; glyph positionRead the color chosen for this glyph.
getXOffset(x, y) / getYOffset(x, y)Glyph position in GUI unitsRead the displacement used when drawing.
TextEffectClock.at(milliseconds)Preview time in millisecondsTemporarily evaluate an effect at a specific time; use try-with-resources to restore the previous clock.
colorSpeed / moveSpeedFinite effect-specific controlsAdjust the selected effect’s color and movement behavior. Geometry settings remain independent of playback speed.
animationSpeedFinite multiplier from -32 to 32Change playback speed; a negative value reverses time and zero freezes it.
optionsMap of supported setting names to valuesOverride matching keys in the effect descriptor. Unsupported names and invalid ranges are rejected.

When you finish: An effect value itself has no registration to remove. If you register it under a formatting trigger, keep and close that registration’s receipt. Always close a temporary clock scope, including when drawing or inspection throws.

Choose one of the 28 built-in effects

Pass one of these lowercase IDs to MovementRegistry.create to build an effect, or use it in a configuration or inline code. wave and none select different modes of DynamicEffect, so 28 IDs cover 27 classes.

Named presets use the names in your configuration. The default matrix preset uses glitch, while digital uses matrix_rain.

What each effect does

A glyph is one drawable character shape. GUI pixels are coordinates after Minecraft applies its interface scale. A segment is a consecutive run sharing an effect and its relevant outline state.

Direct constructors may keep the palette list you supply or apply their own defaults. MovementRegistry validates and copies a nonempty palette before creating an effect. Each class explains its constructor behavior.

What happens to a palette passed directly to a constructor?
  • Most palette constructors retain the list or array. Later edits can change rendering; coordinate any changes with the render thread. Check the constructor's colors parameter for its null and empty-palette rules.
  • PhoenixEffect takes an immutable copy and rejects null entries. Later edits to the original list do not affect it.
  • TextOutlineEffect, VerticalGradientEffect and Volumetric3DEffect read only the first two colors during construction. They keep those color values, not the list.

BreathEffect

Makes a whole text segment gently grow and shrink while its color brightens and darkens.

The same sine wave controls size and brightness. With the default scaleAmplitude of 0.15, the scale varies between 0.85 and 1.15. Color blends from shadowColor (default #333333) toward the primary palette color. brightnessFloor sets the minimum blend fraction (0.5 by default). The renderer transforms the complete segment around its center, keeping its normal width in the line.

ChromaGlitchEffect

Changes each glyph among palette colors and occasionally nudges it sideways.

Color selection advances in shuffleMs windows (150 milliseconds by default). Displacement uses a separate jitterMs window (100 milliseconds), a glyph-dependent seed and a default 0.12 glitch probability. All samples of one glyph share its seed, so its four corners do not tear apart. No colored echo layers are requested.

ChromaWaveEffect

Slides a rainbow color field across otherwise stationary text.

Horizontal position divided by wavelength (default 125 GUI pixels) supplies spatial hue. Time subtracts a colorSpeed-dependent phase. Hue wraps around the color wheel; saturation and brightness both default to one. Geometry remains unchanged.

CompressEffect

Alternates horizontal stretching with vertical compression for the complete segment.

Both axes use the same sine phase, but one adds its amplitude while the other subtracts it. Defaults are 0.3 for horizontal scale amplitude and 0.2 for vertical scale amplitude. The native renderer uses one segment center so the word deforms as a unit while its measured width remains stable.

CustomItalicEffect

Leans the top of each glyph sideways using a configurable slant.

This object exposes slantFactor to the native renderer. The renderer shifts a vertex according to its height above the glyph baseline; returning zero positional offsets here avoids applying the slant twice. The slant option overrides the constructor value.

DiscordGradientEffect

Paints a stationary horizontal gradient through the supplied palette.

The default span is 80 GUI pixels. Within each span, interpolation moves from the first palette entry toward the last, then starts again at the next span. This differs from a cyclic gradient that smoothly interpolates the final entry back to the first. Constructor speed arguments are accepted for factory compatibility and are not used.

DynamicEffect

Provides a vertical wave for wave and a stationary color pattern for none.

In wave mode, colors flow through the palette while letters move up and down along a sine wave. In none mode, the letters and palette stay still; colorSpeed controls the width of the repeating color pattern instead. Mode strings must match exactly: only wave enables vertical motion and only none selects the stationary palette branch.

GlitchEffect

Adds brief, repeatable glyph jumps and color flashes to a flowing gradient.

Each jitterMs interval holds one set of decisions (50 milliseconds by default). Separate seed constants distinguish horizontal jumps, vertical jumps and color flashes for each glyph. Positive moveSpeed enables these changes; zero or negative values disable them while the gradient can keep flowing.

Default displacement amplitude is two GUI pixels. The default jump threshold is 0.05 * moveSpeed and the default flash threshold is 0.1 * moveSpeed. The glitchChance and colorGlitchChance options override these thresholds; a threshold above one always passes.

GradientEffect

Cycles smoothly through an RGB palette while optionally borrowing another registered effect's movement.

After the last palette color, the gradient blends back into the first. Time is measured in seconds, and span sets the horizontal cycle length (100 GUI pixels by default). A negative combined time/position phase wraps into the same cycle before selecting colors. An empty palette leaves the incoming color unchanged. Each offset query looks up the movement by identity; a missing movement adds no displacement.

LetterSpacingEffect

Changes the space between glyphs without stretching their shapes.

ChromaticText.advance adds this effect's spacing to the normal glyph width when placing the next glyph. The position callbacks return zero because layout already includes the extra space. The spacing option overrides the constructor value; negative values bring glyphs closer together.

LiquidPlasmaEffect

Produces a rainbow plasma field from three overlapping sine waves.

Two waves follow horizontal and vertical positions and the third follows their diagonal sum. The horizontal coordinate starts at the current segment origin. Their combined value becomes hue; fieldScale, diagonalScale, saturation, brightness and hueOffset tune the field. This changes color only, with no vertex displacement.

MatrixRainEffect

Keeps a readable foreground word while separate seeded code streams appear above and below it.

A Cell describes one background symbol; the native font supplies its actual shape. Each column/side has a stable seed, draw/erase phase, head position and sparse spinner cells. The renderer packs cells using MatrixGrid and preserves the foreground text. Rows and reach bound the background area; inline definitions receive stricter row limits than normal configuration. Matrix reveal/shuffle behavior is informed by glmatrix; its permission notice is bundled in LICENSES.

MatrixSpinEffect

Simulates a whole-segment flip by taking the cosine of a shared rotation angle.

The cosine controls horizontal scale and chooses front/back colors. Its sign can become negative, producing a mirror image. The scale is kept at least 0.001 away from zero in magnitude to avoid a degenerate transform at the exact edge-on phase. Vertical scale stays one.

MirroredGradientEffect

Reflects a stationary palette pattern around the middle of each horizontal span.

Position is measured from the current segment origin and clamped at its left edge. The latter half of each span folds back toward the first half before palette sampling. The default span is 100 GUI pixels. No time-dependent color speed or geometry offset is introduced.

PhoenixEffect

Combines a looping palette gradient with a vertical sine-wave movement.

Color and movement speeds are independent. A zero movement speed returns an exact zero offset; a zero color speed leaves spatial palette variation visible. Unlike most direct palette constructors, this constructor copies the palette so later list edits cannot change it.

PulseEffect

Moves the entire row of glyphs up and down while its palette flows horizontally.

All glyphs share the same vertical phase because the offset depends on time rather than x. Time in seconds is multiplied by moveSpeed and three; amplitudeY defaults to two GUI pixels. This is translation, not a change in glyph size.

RainbowWaveEffect

Combines a segment-relative rainbow color field with a traveling vertical wave.

Color uses local x within the current segment, while the vertical wave samples the incoming x coordinate. Palette arguments are not needed: hue is generated directly with saturation (default 0.85) and brightness (default one). Wave amplitude defaults to two GUI pixels; color and wave speeds are independently retained.

ScaleEffect

Changes glyph size and its measured advance using a fixed uniform multiplier.

The scale option overrides the constructor value. ChromaticText.advance uses the same uniform scale so width, wrapping and drawing remain aligned. This is a per-glyph size effect, unlike whole-segment breathing whose nominal flow width stays unchanged.

ShiverEffect

Jitters each glyph independently in both axes, holding its position until the next jitter interval.

Each jitterMs interval holds one position (100 milliseconds by default). The seed includes the glyph identity, and separate constants distinguish horizontal and vertical choices, so letters can move independently. The default amplitude is the magnitude of moveSpeed in GUI pixels. A moveSpeed of zero disables motion, even when amplitude options are set.

StaticRainbowEffect

Cycles the whole text through one shared palette color without moving its glyphs.

The palette helper always receives spatial position zero, so every glyph samples the same color at a given time. Despite the class name, nonzero colorSpeed still animates the color. moveSpeed is retained for source compatibility but is not used by these callbacks.

StretchEffect

Stretches and relaxes a whole text segment horizontally around its center.

A sine wave varies the horizontal scale by scaleAmplitudeX (0.5 by default). The primary palette color stays fixed and vertical scale stays at one. The renderer transforms the segment as a unit, keeping its normal width in the line instead of changing the spacing after each letter.

TextOutlineEffect

Selects a foreground color and a separate outline decoration.

The first palette entry colors the text and the second colors the outline; missing entries use white and black. The native renderer draws neighboring offset passes before the foreground, using outlineRadius (default one GUI pixel). It can keep this decoration alongside a different primary effect.

VerticalGradientEffect

Assigns distinct colors to the top and bottom of each native glyph.

The native renderer recognizes this concrete effect and samples getTopColor/getBottomColor for the vertex corners. Its ordinary color callback returns the top color as a fallback for consumers that do not implement vertex gradients. Missing palette entries default to white and #AAAAAA.

VerticalShearEffect

Raises or lowers points across a complete segment in proportion to horizontal distance.

The slope is GUI pixels of vertical change per horizontal GUI pixel. The constructor uses -0.2 when given zero; an explicit slope option can override that default. The native renderer handles this concrete effect as a shear transform, avoiding duplicate per-glyph displacement.

Volumetric3DEffect

Adds offset background layers that make text look extruded.

Foreground and side colors are independent. The constructor's depth argument sets the layer count: positive values are truncated to an integer and nonpositive values use five. When configuring the effect, layers sets the number of background samples, while depth/angle or extensionX/extensionY set the total distance and direction. The renderer draws the farthest layers first, then the foreground.

WobbleEffect

Moves glyphs along independent horizontal and vertical waves.

Horizontal sine and vertical cosine use different clock multipliers and wavelengths. Defaults are amplitudes 1.2 and 1.4 GUI pixels with wavelengths 4Ï€ and 5Ï€ GUI pixels. A fixed primary color keeps the motion easy to see; glyph scale stays unchanged.

WordFadeEffect

Fades the foreground from left to right across its current text segment.

Position is measured from the segment start. span defaults to the segment width when that width is positive, or 120 GUI pixels otherwise. fadeStart and fadeEnd are fractions of that span: zero is its start and one is its end. minAlpha sets the lowest fade multiplier (0.15 by default). The renderer multiplies each vertex's alpha by the value from getDynamicAlpha and by the base opacity multiplier separately.

Find the settings an effect accepts

The meaning of colorSpeed and moveSpeed depends on the selected movement. For these effects, moveSpeed controls geometry:

  • size uses a positive moveSpeed as the scale multiplier; zero or negative values select 1.5. The explicit scale option overrides it.
  • spacing uses moveSpeed as extra GUI pixels after each glyph. Zero selects 2; negative values reduce spacing. The explicit spacing option can set zero without selecting the fallback.
  • slant uses moveSpeed as the horizontal shift per GUI pixel above the glyph baseline. Zero selects 0.25. The explicit slant option can set zero.
  • 3d uses moveSpeed as its constructor layer count, not a distance. Use layers for the number of background passes and depth for their total reach in GUI pixels; see extrusion geometry.

Use the separate animationSpeed control to change playback without changing geometry. A value of 0.5 plays at half speed, zero samples the initial frame and negative values run time backward. Built-in factories such as chroma and outline ignore both constructor speed controls; animationSpeed still scales the time seen by any animated callbacks.

A playback-speed setting may return a TimedEffect around the effect you created. Use TimedEffect.base(effect) to retrieve the underlying effect before checking its class or inspecting its supported settings. See TimedEffect, TimedEffect.base(effect).

On a ConfigurableTextEffect, parameters() lists the name, bounds, units and type of each supported option. settings() returns values you have explicitly set. Other options use the effect's defaults, so an empty map does not mean that every value is zero. Each class documents its defaults and formulas.

Creating an effect also checks relationships between settings. For example, span and wavelength must be greater than zero even where their individual rules list zero as the minimum. For a fade, fadeEnd must be greater than fadeStart. A settings table alone cannot express all these checks.

Descriptor options follow a semicolon, for example 3d;depth=10;angle=225;layers=16. Explicit API option maps override matching descriptor keys. Unknown keys, invalid number types/ranges, reversed fade bounds, and inconsistent scale bounds fail validation. Inline definitions also have smaller work budgets.

For a new effect, implement IChromaticEffect and register its callbacks. The interface explains sampling, animation time and shared-instance rules.

Getting started · Formatting syntax · Troubleshooting

Write a function that colors text red

This custom callback keeps position and size unchanged and supplies a fixed red foreground. Replace the sample expression with your own animation while retaining finite output.

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.IChromaticEffect;
IChromaticEffect custom = new IChromaticEffect() {
    @Override public int getRenderColor(int original, float x, float y) { return 0xFF0000; }
    @Override public float getXOffset(float x, float y) { return 0; }
    @Override public float getYOffset(float x, float y) { return 0; }
};

val custom = object : IChromaticEffect {
    override fun getRenderColor(original: Int, x: Float, y: Float) = 0xFF0000
    override fun getXOffset(x: Float, y: Float) = 0f
    override fun getYOffset(x: Float, y: Float) = 0f
}

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.IChromaticEffect
def custom = [
    getRenderColor: { int original, float x, float y -> 0xFF0000 },
    getXOffset: { float x, float y -> 0f },
    getYOffset: { float x, float y -> 0f }
] as IChromaticEffect

val custom = new net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.IChromaticEffect:
  override def getRenderColor(original: Int, x: Float, y: Float): Int = 0xFF0000
  override def getXOffset(x: Float, y: Float): Float = 0f
  override def getYOffset(x: Float, y: Float): Float = 0f

val custom = Text.custom(function(channel, x, y, original, fallback, milliseconds) {
    if (channel == "color") return 16711680.0;
    return fallback;
});
Text.namedEffect("my_pack:red", "red", custom);

ZenScript channels cover color, x/y offsets, opacity, uniform and axis scales, outline/color, static/animated classifications, horizontal blending, passthrough and whole-segment transforms. Return fallback for channels you do not change. Generic callbacks cannot manufacture the concrete volumetric layer geometry; use the registered 3d preset for that. The script callback is shared by reference and may be sampled by common-side layout code, so keep it free of client-only assumptions and registry mutation.

Preview an animation at a fixed time

The example samples the animation at a chosen time, making screenshots or comparisons repeatable. The temporary clock setting applies only to the calling thread and is restored when the block returns or throws. Playback speed still multiplies the time seen by the effect.

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TextEffectClock;
try (var sample = TextEffectClock.at(250.0)) {
    int rgb = effect.getRenderColor(0xFFFFFF, 10, 20);
}

atEffectTime(250.0) {
    val rgb = effect.getRenderColor(0xFFFFFF, 10f, 20f)
}

import net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.TextEffectClock
def sample = TextEffectClock.at(250d)
try { def rgb = effect.getRenderColor(0xFFFFFF, 10f, 20f) }
finally { sample.close() }

atTime(250.0) {
  val rgb = effect.getRenderColor(0xFFFFFF, 10f, 20f)
}

Text.atTime(250.0, function() {
    val width = Text.compile("&[warm_wave]ABC").width(function(character) { return 6; });
    print(width);
});

Keep the work synchronous and on the same thread. A clock scope does not make arbitrary mutable callbacks thread-safe. Layout-only sampling does not allocate GPU resources.
